Art lacks an objective definition, though a case for objective judgment on ["good" or "bad](https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=lNI07egoefc) art can be made.

Instead of trying to define what art is, or what art should be, or what is "good" or "bad" art, we should examine art through with an emphasis on historical context.

In this way we can quickly discover that art has always been a reflection of society. Whether it be pre-historic funeral masks and fertility figurines, mythological scenes, religious patronage, idyllic landscapes, war-torn battlefields, or chaotic bursts or color without form, one can virtually always make a case that art is a mirror.

Art as a mirror, including art forms not traditionally included in Art History, should perhaps be *THE* definition of the field in question.
